name: FKA twigs
label: Young/Atlantic
lede: Tahliah Barnett spent her early twenties dancing behind Jessie J and Kylie Minogue, then released a video of her own face that 16 million people watched. Years later she won a Grammy for a techno-leaning record made after she moved to Prague.

eras.title: The girl in the back of the video
eras.text: Barnett came out of Cheltenham and the BRIT School as a dancer, working behind other people's hits while she figured out her own sound. By the end of 2012 she had a new name and a first EP on Bandcamp.

years.h: Kylie Minogue, Ed Sheeran and Jessie J all have her dancing behind them
years.p: Before she sang a note in public, Tahliah Barnett danced in videos for Kylie Minogue, Plan B, Ed Sheeran, Taio Cruz, Wretch 32 and Jessie J, including "Do It like a Dude" and "Price Tag".
years.xp:
Barnett grew up in Cheltenham, won a scholarship to St Edward's School, then went to the BRIT School in South London at 17 to study dance, and later studied fine art at Croydon College. Per Wikipedia, she also worked as a hostess in a strip club and sang at The Box Soho while she was getting started.

The video work paid, but the songs she was writing on the side were the point.

years.h: Another act called the Twigs asks her to change it
years.p: She was nicknamed "Twigs" for her cracking joints. When a twin-sister act using the same name objected, she added "FKA".
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Barnett says FKA is just three letters, not an acronym.

years.h: EP1 goes up on Bandcamp, each song with its own video
years.p: She released EP1 herself and posted the individual music videos to YouTube one by one.

eras.title: Water Me
eras.text: Jesse Kanda's video for "Water Me" made her a name, EP2 put her on Young Turks, and LP1 got her shortlisted for the Mercury Prize. Arca and a rotating cast of producers built a sound that was quiet, strange and loud in its feelings.

years.h: Jesse Kanda's "Water Me" video collects 16 million views
years.p: Kanda directed, with twigs credited as co-director. Wikipedia puts the YouTube count at over sixteen million.
years.xp:
The Guardian named her New Band of the Day that August. The video's slow, morphing close-up of her face did most of the introducing.

Kanda kept directing her videos, including "How's That" from the same EP.

years.h: EP2 lands on Young Turks
years.p: "How's That", "Papi Pacify", "Water Me" and "Ultraviolet", four songs made with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]]. Pitchfork gave it 8 out of 10.
years.xp: Dummy named it Album of the Week, while The Line of Best Fit was cooler on it at 6 out of 10, per Wikipedia's reception box. It came out on Young Turks, the label that would release her first three records.

years.cap: FKA twigs at Laneway Festival, Sydney
years.h: BBC puts her on the Sound of 2014 list
years.p: She was a BBC Sound of 2014 nominee, and also turned up on Spotify's and Billboard's lists of acts to watch.

years.cap: FKA twigs at Webster Hall, New York, August 2014
years.h: LP1 debuts at No. 16 in the UK
years.p: Her first album was recorded over 2013-14 with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]], [[Clams Casino|772a0eb3-fe31-4a08-b583-690296f44900]], [[Paul Epworth|65380f7e-cb7a-4594-ae44-28ff55160746]], [[Devonte Hynes|68eb8831-4d0b-4a2b-9209-3ccade5117f0]], [[Emile Haynie|d6f3c7d7-3c95-4bf6-8647-0efeec36d704]] and [[Sampha|130c2184-14f2-4180-a216-04b5a333be57]]. Pitchfork gave it 8.8.
years.xp:
LP1 debuted at No. 30 on the Billboard 200 as well, with first-week US sales of 10,370 copies, per Wikipedia. It was shortlisted for the Mercury Prize in September and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Recording Package.

Time and Clash both ranked it the best album of 2014. Singles: "Two Weeks" (June 24), "Pendulum" and "Video Girl" (October).

eras.title: Melissa, and a body that wouldn't cooperate
eras.text: With M3LL155X she directed a 16-minute film and moved the music toward theater. Then came a long quiet stretch: a fibroid surgery, an ASAP Rocky feature and ads she directed and starred in.

years.cap: FKA twigs live at Paradiso, Amsterdam, March 2015
years.h: Congregata fills the Roundhouse, months before a new record
years.p: A theatrical performance staged at London's Roundhouse in Camden in February 2015, ahead of M3LL155X.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Congregata as a theatrical performance at the Roundhouse in February 2015. The photo above is from her Paradiso show in Amsterdam a few weeks later.

years.cap: FKA twigs live in Berlin, March 2015
years.h: M3LL155X comes with a 16-minute film attached
years.p: Four songs with Boots, and a self-directed film in which Michèle Lamy plays an anglerfish. Pitchfork gave it 8.6.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the EP explores "Melissa," her name for her own female energy, which she describes as a creative force rather than an alter ego. Metacritic collected 12 reviews for an 89. The film drew two MTV Video Music Award nominations in 2016, for visual effects and choreography.

years.h: Fibroid surgery, after what she called "a fruit bowl of pain every day"
years.p: She had surgery for fibroid tumours in December 2017 and later described living with them that way, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: In 2020 she adopted a vegan diet after finding that animal products made the fibroid symptoms worse, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Magdalene
eras.text: Heartbreak and a rebuilt body became choral, distorted, sometimes operatic pop.

years.h: "Cellophane" climbs a pole, then falls into a clay underworld
years.p: Andrew Thomas Huang directed: twigs climbs a pole to meet a creature with her face, falls, and is covered in clay.
years.xp:
Pitchfork made it Best New Track and its best song of 2019; The Guardian ranked it No. 6. Critics singled out the vocal, which one described as cracking and groaning as if dragging more weight than it can bear.

Several publications linked the song to her ended engagement to Robert Pattinson; twigs herself has described the album as about how heartbreak could be so all-encompassing, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Magdalene arrives five years after LP1
years.p: Recorded across 2016-2019 with [[Nicolas Jaar|06e99a1b-4020-4380-ab27-1a3e0c5e557c]] and a long list of producers, including [[Skrillex|ae002c5d-aac6-490b-a39a-30aa9e2edf2b]], [[Jack Antonoff|1155a7a9-a7b4-46ba-ba27-6b6c98be487e]], [[Daniel Lopatin|d5cd6528-3185-4f1b-a297-807b00b16f83]] and [[Koreless|ec0bfe7d-fc42-43c7-a2ea-dbf33a869ba3]]. Pitchfork gave it 9.4 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
Metacritic's score is 88 from 28 reviews. "Holy Terrain" features [[Future|48262e82-db9f-4a92-b650-dfef979b73ec]]; the singles were "Cellophane" (April 24), "Holy Terrain" (September 9), "Home with You" (October 7) and "Sad Day" (November 4), per Wikipedia.

It was No. 1 on the year-end lists of The A.V. Club, Clash, Now and Time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shia LaBeouf · Wikipedia: FKA twigs
years.h: twigs sues Shia LaBeouf in Los Angeles; the case settles in 2025
years.p: She filed in Los Angeles Superior Court in December 2020, alleging sexual battery, assault and emotional distress. LaBeouf denied the allegations.
years.xp: The two met on the set of Honey Boy and dated from mid-2018 to mid-2019, per Wikipedia. According to reporting cited there, LaBeouf first said he was "abusive" and expressed remorse, then denied the allegations. The case was set for trial several times and settled in July 2025 on confidential terms.

eras.title: Caprisongs
eras.text: She kept her Young imprint, and made a mixtape by phone: DMs, FaceTimes and friends leaving voice notes. Critics kept it near the tops of their lists.

years.h: She signs to Atlantic Records
years.p: Her first release on the label is "Tears in the Club", out December 16.

years.h: The Weeknd watches from the club while she dances in a fish tank
years.p: Amber Grace Johnson directed the "Tears in the Club" video, which has twigs dancing in a club and performing in a fish tank with [[The Weeknd|c8b03190-306c-4120-bb0b-6f2ebfc06ea9]] looking on.
years.xp: Writers include Tahliah Barnett, Abel Tesfaye, Ali Tamposi, Henry Walter, Alejandra Ghersi and Pablo Diaz-Reixa; producers were [[Cirkut|0eb93ee5-2e6a-4ab4-a988-99c9139a664a]], [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]] and [[El Guincho|7e57d8a2-e6eb-48dd-8e50-ff7eaa412ccb]]. It peaked at No. 12 in New Zealand and No. 79 in Canada, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Caprisongs lands on Young/Atlantic
years.p: A mixtape with [[Pa Salieu|03100b87-7d27-4d56-b049-2007599656cc]], [[Daniel Caesar|b46e298d-d3a5-4695-a03e-63e8c523b23e]], [[Rema|720c46ba-a0e4-4b58-aee2-3bd70c70901f]], [[Jorja Smith|d62614aa-ef2c-44cd-8a7b-91292755a1d0]], [[Unknown T|a688dc7a-c743-4ec2-9355-c3dcdb30bf0e]], Dystopia, [[Shygirl|9385f1a7-8623-4d0c-b171-f1e6e87220c5]] and The Weeknd. Pitchfork gave it 7.8.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, Metacritic scores it 80 from 17 reviews; it peaked at No. 91 on the Billboard 200 and topped the US Top Dance Albums chart. El Guincho executive-produced alongside twigs, with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]], [[Mike Dean|73e36439-1e9a-4925-bf2c-1d7f7885fbb0]] and Cirkut on the boards.

Rolling Stone ranked it No. 8 of 2022, Slant No. 4 and Entertainment Weekly No. 3.

years.big: curated primarily through DMs and Facetimes
q: curated primarily through DMs and Facetimes
years.h: Friends' voice notes become the glue between songs
years.p: NPR's review calls the mixtape a first for her, made with El Guincho and pulling from synth-pop, dancehall, grime, neo-soul and ambient.
years.xp: The review singles out the voice messages from friends that sit between the songs, and reads them as the scaffolding for a record where she drops the guarded avatar.

years.h: NME hands her the Godlike Genius award
years.p: At the 2022 BandLab NME Awards she performed "Meta Angel" and "Tears in the Club", then took the Godlike Genius prize.

years.src: NPR: FKA twigs Tiny Desk · Wikipedia: FKA twigs
years.h: "Killer" gets its first airing in a church
years.p: At London's St. Matthias Church she played "home with you", "killer" and "cellophane" with piano, double bass, violin and cello.
years.xp:
NPR's framing had her performing amid "flames of offering" in a sermon on the perils of devotion, and called her "a new-age priestess". Kelly Nicole Moran played piano, Damsel Elysium double bass and violin, Lucinda Chua cello.

"Killer" had not been released; its video followed on July 20, directed by Yoann Lemoine with Aron Piper on a Portuguese beach, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Caprisongs · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2022
years.h: Pitchfork puts Caprisongs at No. 24 for 2022
years.p: It placed 24th on Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2022, after a 7.8 review in January.
years.xp: The 7.8 score comes from Wikipedia's reception box for the album. The rank is on Pitchfork's list as reproduced by yearendlists.com.

eras.title: Eusexua, and the Grammy
eras.text: She used the gap between records to perform in couture, argue with an ad regulator and testify to the Senate. The record that followed won a Grammy.

years.h: She debuts "Unearth Her" on a Valentino runway
years.p: The song premiered at Valentino's Paris Fashion Week show in 2023; the producer was [[Koreless|ec0bfe7d-fc42-43c7-a2ea-dbf33a869ba3]].

years.h: 85 demos leak, and she steps back from releasing
years.p: After 85 demo tracks leaked, she announced a pause in new releases.

years.h: The ad regulator bans a Calvin Klein ad, then reverses itself
years.p: The UK Advertising Standards Authority banned the semi-nude ad in January and revoked the ban in March. Twigs said she was proud of her physicality.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the ASA revoked the ban after a climbdown.

years.h: She testifies to the Senate about AI and deepfakes
years.p: Barnett appeared before the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Intellectual Property.

years.cap: FKA twigs live at We Love Green, Paris, June 2025
years.h: Prague techno becomes the album Eusexua
years.p: Made across 2022-24 with [[Koreless|ec0bfe7d-fc42-43c7-a2ea-dbf33a869ba3]]. Pitchfork gave it 9.1.
years.xp:
She moved to Prague and fell into the city's techno scene while making it. Twigs told British Vogue the word describes the sensation of being so euphoric you could transcend human form, per Wikipedia.

Metacritic scores it 87 from 24 reviews. It was nominated for the Mercury Prize and lost to Sam Fender's People Watching.

years.h: The brief she gave herself for a techno record
years.p: Her description of the sound she was after, per Wikipedia's article on the album.
years.xp: She has said the record keeps the spirit of techno without being techno in the strict sense. Rich Juzwiak's Pitchfork review compared it to Madonna's Ray of Light and called it a masterful pop-star moment.

years.h: Eusexua: Afterglow follows in November
years.p: A reissue on Young/Atlantic, with "Cheap Hotel" and "Predictable Girl" as singles. Pitchfork scored it 8.0.

years.cap: FKA twigs lifted by a dancer, Adidas Arena, Paris, June 2026
years.h: Eusexua wins the Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album
years.p: The award came at the 68th Annual Grammy Awards, per Wikipedia.
